core_concept: This document explains three common methods for styling HTML elements: internal CSS, external CSS, and inline CSS. Internal CSS involves embedding CSS rules within `<style>` tags in the `<head>` of an HTML document, while external CSS uses separate `.css` files linked to the HTML. Inline CSS applies styles directly to individual HTML elements using the `style` attribute, though this approach is generally discouraged due to potential maintenance issues.
technical_breakdown: CSS styling is used to control the visual presentation of HTML documents.
There are three primary methods for applying CSS: internal, external, and inline.
Each method has its advantages and disadvantages regarding maintainability, scalability, and potential for conflicts.
